title: Give a retail tenant a disclosure statement
what: Give the tenant a disclosure statement, setting out the lease's costs and terms, before a retail shop lease is entered into.

sources.title: Retail Leases Act 1994 (NSW)
sources.publisher: NSW Legislation (via the Open Australian Legal Corpus)
sources.quote: (1) At least 7 days before a retail shop lease is entered into, the lessor must give the lessee a disclosure statement for the lease (the lessor's disclosure statement)

triggers.note: Before a retail shop lease is entered into (and, in some states, before a renewal).

reach.note: Landlords of retail shops: chiefly non-residential property operators (class 6712); any business that leases out a retail shop is covered.

confidence_note: Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the version shown (DECISIONS E-118); later changes not checked.

assessment.summary: Before a retail shop lease is signed, the landlord must give the tenant a disclosure statement setting out the lease's costs and terms. It informs small retail tenants, at some cost to landlords.

marks.reason: Tenants learn a lease's full costs before signing, which strengthens small retailers' bargaining with large landlords.
Landlords must prepare and update a prescribed statement for each lease.
